sections.h2: Where to send or drop off a deed
sections.html:
Recording packages are accepted by mail or courier at 400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307. USPS, UPS and FedEx all work. The phone is (231) 592-0148. Call first to learn the counter's recording hours.

The register maintains the real estate record for every parcel in Mecosta County. Indexing is complete back to January 1, 1968, and every document back to 1859 has been scanned and tagged by liber and page. Index books, including oil and gas, are imaged on the Countyfusion site, and a second public search runs through Vanguard at mecosta.mi.publicsearch.us.

Wherever the parcel sits, the deed is filed in Big Rapids, while assessing and collection stay with the township, village or city. Work out which local unit covers the parcel before asking for a payoff or tax certificate.

sections.h2: Selling a home in Mecosta County
sections.html:
The county has 16 townships, the city of Big Rapids and four villages: Barryton, Mecosta, Morley and Stanwood. Big Rapids is the county seat and largest city, home to Ferris State University.

The county had an estimated 42,320 people in mid-2025, up 4.9 percent from 2020. Owners live in 76.9 percent of homes, and a typical house is valued near $178,900.

Recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, affidavit or similar instrument costs $30.00. That amount includes the statutory fee under MCL 600.2567a plus a $5.00 contribution to the automation fund. A document releasing several instruments adds $3.00 for each extra one.

Mecosta County Register of Deeds price list
ServicePrice
Deed or mortgage recording$30.00
Tax certificate with a warranty deed, up to five descriptions$5.00 per instrument
Each description beyond five$0.20
Copy of a land record, each page$1.00
Copy of a plat, each page$2.00
Name search$0.50 per year, $5.00 minimum
Certifying a record copy$5.00

The office also records fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral under the Uniform Commercial Code. All other personal property filings belong with the Secretary of State.

Two levies add together here. Mecosta County charges 55 cents per $500 slice of value and the state charges $3.75 per slice (MCL 207.525), with any partial slice counted as whole. A deed valued at $100 or more is taxable, and MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor.

The Register of Deeds office collects both amounts alongside the recording fee, and the act calls for payment inside 15 days of delivering the deed.

The deed has to carry the property's full value. Alternatively, attach a valuation affidavit and add a line on the deed saying it is on file, which costs nothing to file. Claim any MCL 207.526 exemption on the deed's face, for instance for a parent-to-child transfer or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.

An eleven-point checklist drawn from Michigan statutes governs what gets filed. These are the points that most often cause trouble:

  • Names printed under the signatures that differ from the notary acknowledgment
  • A missing grantee address, or no name and address for the drafter
  • A notary block with no commission expiration date
  • A deed naming a surviving owner without a certified death certificate on record
  • A court order lacking the clerk's certification and seal
  • Type under 10 point, or less than 2 1/2 inches of clear top margin
  • An opening line naming more than one recordable event
  • No statement of total property value and no affidavit

Stock should be white and 20-pound, from letter to legal size. Run through the list before mailing, since a rejected package costs days.

sections.h2: Do you need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract and an assignment of a land contract all do. The certificate comes from the county treasurer and shows taxes paid for the five years before the instrument date, under MCL 211.135. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

Unpaid taxes move toward forfeiture and foreclosure, so a seller carrying old bills should ask for a payoff figure before closing. Payoffs and certificates are usually handled by the title company out of sale proceeds, which keeps a cash sale moving without extra trips to the courthouse.

The register records only the real-estate side of Uniform Commercial Code work: fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral. A standard-form filing with two debtor names and up to 100 pages is $30.00. Extra charges apply for a non-standard form ($7.00), for filings over 100 pages ($12.00) and for each debtor name past two ($10.00).

  • UCC search, per name: $6.00
  • State or federal tax lien certificate, per name: $3.00
  • Copy of a UCC filing, per page: $2.00
  • Copy of a state or federal tax lien, per page: $1.00

UCC search results cover personal property filings only through June 30, 2001. Real estate filings made after July 1, 2001 appear in the real estate index. Searches are done as time allows and carry no guarantee.

The Equalization page links a land records portal and a map viewer, and it carries tax maps for each of the 16 townships: Aetna, Austin, Big Rapids, Chippewa, Colfax, Deerfield, Fork, Grant, Green, Hinton, Martiny, Mecosta, Millbrook, Morton, Sheridan and Wheatland. Its document center also lists the millage rates and a property tax estimator.

Lining up the parcel number on a tax map with the legal description on the deed is a quick way to catch a wrong lot before closing. Documents back to 1859 are imaged, which helps when an old lot line or easement turns up in a title search. The Vanguard support line is (888) 608-1808.

sections.h2: Steps for recording a sale deed
sections.html:
A typical sale follows this order. The title company drafts or reviews the deed and checks it against the rejection list above. You sign before a notary, and the notary block needs a commission expiration date. If the deed carries warranties, the county treasurer issues the tax certificate. The package then goes to 400 Elm Street with the $30.00 fee, any certificate charge and the transfer tax.

Bring or include the full property value on the deed, or a valuation affidavit with a line on the deed saying it is on file. Once recorded, the deed appears in the index and the register reports the transfer so the assessors can update the parcel. Ask the closing agent for a copy of the recorded deed afterward and keep it with your sale papers.

faqs.q: What is Mecosta County's charge for filing a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per instrument, plus $3.00 for each additional instrument released in the same paper. Page copies are $1.00 each.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Mecosta County sale?
faqs.a: The state charges $3.75 and the county 55 cents for each $500 of value, with a partial slice counted as whole. The seller pays unless an exemption is stated on the deed.

faqs.q: What address takes Mecosta County recording packages?
faqs.a: 400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307. Phone (231) 592-0148 beforehand to confirm paperwork and payment.

faqs.q: Is an uncertified court order good enough for Mecosta County recording?
faqs.a: No. The clerk of the court must certify and seal it. A plain copy is sent back.

faqs.q: How old are the Mecosta County records that can be searched?
faqs.a: The full index starts January 1, 1968, and papers from 1859 onward are scanned and tagged by liber and page. Countyfusion and Vanguard are the two public portals.
